text: A is attack, built for hitting targets on land or at sea. B is bomber. C is cargo. F is fighter.
The Air Force even gave the F to the F one seventeen Nighthawk, a stealth jet built for ground attack, with no official air-to-air role.
For years, people were convinced a secret F nineteen stealth fighter existed. In July nineteen eighty-six, the Air Force sealed off a crash site in California, and the rumors exploded.
The rest of the list works the same way. W is weather reconnaissance, which is why the Air Force's hurricane hunters are W C one thirties.
And M and U look alike, but they're split by the kind of mission. M aircraft fly combat and special operations. U aircraft fly support, like the U H sixty Black Hawk.
The F forty-seven was chosen partly to honor the P forty-seven Thunderbolt, and nineteen forty-seven, the year the Air Force was founded.
